statement.p: Find the total area enclosed by the cardioid r=4-\cos\theta shown in the following figure:

static.solution:
r=4 - \cos \theta in r and \theta (cartesian, not polar, this time):
r_0=3 ,\quad r_1=4 \quad r_2=5
We see that as \theta varies from 0 to \pi, the radius r increases from 3 to 5,
so we get the upper half of the cardioid (the lower half is obtained as \theta varies from \pi to 2\pi and consequently r decreases from 5 to 3.
Since the cardioid is symmetric with respect to the x-axis we may compute the upper area and double the result.
Using \cos^{2}\theta =\frac{ \cos 2\theta +1}{2} we get A = 2\cdot \frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{\pi }{r}^{2} \,d\theta= \int_{0}^{\pi }{\left(4- \cos \theta \right)}^{2} \,d\theta= \int_{0}^{\pi}\left(16-8 \cos \theta +\cos^{2}\theta \right) \,d\theta= \int_{0}^{\pi}\left(16-8 \cos \theta +\frac{ \cos 2\theta +1}{2}\right)\,d\theta=\int_{0}^{\pi }\left(\frac{33}{2}-8 \cos \theta +\frac{1}{2} \cos 2\theta \right) \,d\theta = \frac{33}{2}\theta -8 \sin \theta +\frac{1}{4} \sin 2\theta \bigg|_{0}^{\pi }= \frac{33\pi }{2}
